facts.text: Fairfield is the county seat and the only incorporated city in Camas County, Idaho.
The Oregon Short Line Railroad arrived in 1911, turning Fairfield and Hill City into prairie hubs and briefly making the region the sheep‑shipping capital of the world.
A 19th‑century emigrant group hired explorer Tim Goodale to guide them along a shortcut from Fort Hall to Boise, passing through what would become Fairfield.
Historic Sanborn maps from 1915 to 1931 show Fairfield’s downtown blocks, schools, hotels, factories, churches, and storefronts, revealing everyday life over a century ago.
These real old maps let visitors see Fairfield exactly as it looked more than a century ago, bringing local history to life in ways books cannot.
Families use Fairfield’s historic maps to reconnect with ancestry, remember hometowns, or give personal gifts tied to meaningful places.
